name: Toad Pedophile
caption: The satire's own ring announcer and host, on-air across nearly every chapter of the [DEWF/WCWF] series -- the closest thing the run has to a viewpoint character, and the only one the text has address the author directly.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (chapters one through soul-doubt), where this character hosts/announces on-camera throughout.

name: Tommy Sledge
caption: A hard-boiled "Private Wrestling Investigator" original to the series, narrating chapter seven and a half as a noir pastiche before resurfacing at the climax of Soul Doubt.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (chapter seven and a half, soul-doubt) -- a hired investigator, not a wrestler/manager/referee/authority-figure/commentator/mascot; no closer-fitting roles value exists.

identity.note: The same billing exists in other wings; no identity join is asserted (bare-name match is insufficient)

name: Vincent B. Baats
caption: The WCWF's own resident "doctor/lawyer/dry cleaner" since 1993, murdered by the Soultaker on-air -- his cloning tanks become the wraparound mystery the whole nine-chapter run resolves.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (chapter syxx, chapter seven, soul-doubt) -- billed as the fed's doctor/lawyer/dry cleaner, none of which is a closer-fitting roles value.

name: Ted DiBiase
caption: Billed as owner, president and promoter of the satire's own revived WCWF -- the anchor role the whole nine-chapter run is staged around.

identity.note: A per-promotion portrayal of the real professional wrestler Ted DiBiase, distinct from any other promotion's own portrayal of the same real wrestler under the per-promotion portrayal doctrine -- never merged across promotions.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (chapters one through soul-doubt), billed throughout as the WCWF's owner/president/promoter.

name: Hulk Hogan
caption: Billed as the WCWF's returning top star and, entering the series, its World Heavyweight Champion -- a title he loses to Shane Douglas via a signed-in-error contract cash-in.

identity.note: A per-promotion portrayal of the real professional wrestler Hulk Hogan, distinct from any other promotion's own portrayal of the same real wrestler under the per-promotion portrayal doctrine -- never merged across promotions.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (one, two, four, five, syxx; namechecked in seven).

name: Shane Douglas
caption: Billed as "The Franchise," self-declared refugee of the rival DEWF -- wins the WCWF World Heavyweight Championship from Hulk Hogan via a mid-match contract cash-in, then loses it by no-show forfeit to Nailz.

identity.note: A per-promotion portrayal of the real professional wrestler Shane Douglas, distinct from any other promotion's own portrayal of the same real wrestler under the per-promotion portrayal doctrine -- never merged across promotions.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (three, four, syxx, seven, seven and a half, soul-doubt).

name: Curt Hennig
caption: Signed on a cash-per-appearance deal and rebranded "Mr. Spiffy" after a lawyer's cameo forbids the WCWF from using "Mr. Perfect" -- co-hosts commentary and manages Nailz through the run.

identity.note: A per-promotion portrayal of the real professional wrestler Curt Hennig, distinct from any other promotion's own portrayal of the same real wrestler under the per-promotion portrayal doctrine -- never merged across promotions.

tenures.source: The [DEWF/WCWF] satire series' own served chapters (syxx, seven, seven and a half, soul-doubt) -- co-commentates and later manages Nailz.
